title: fix(fields): an unreadable lookup reads "Restricted record", not its raw id
body:
Closes #13335
Clause-②: no

## What changed

A lookup / master_detail / tree value whose referenced record the viewer's own read answers "not found" for now reads **"Restricted record"** (translated), with a lock icon, **no record id and no link**. That is the case the card measured: the record GET answers 404 for this viewer, and the ObjectStack adapter's `findOne` turns a 404 into `null`, the `DataSource` contract's "not found". Before, the cell printed the raw id beside a question mark (`UnresolvedReferenceMark`).

**Measured map on `origin/main` (404ccae0d).**
- The grid and the record page share one renderer. `ObjectGrid` columns and `DetailSection` both reach `getCellRenderer('lookup')`, which is `LookupCellRenderer` in `@object-ui/fields`. Nothing else registers `lookup` / `master_detail`.
- The label comes from `useLookupName`: one `findOne` per referenced id, cached in the module-level `lookupNameCache`. The cache records `pending` / `err` / `ok`, but the hook returned only `string | undefined`, so a read that settled with no record and a read still in flight both fell through to `UnresolvedLookupReference`. That component draws the `CircleQuestionMark` icon and the raw id.
- No server-side change is needed. The 404 already reaches the client as `findOne` → `null`.

**The fix (one seam, `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`).**
- `useLookupName` now returns which state it reached: `named` (the name), `absent` (the read settled and there is no record), or `undefined` (not asked, in flight, the read threw, or a record came back that no display field names).
- `LookupCellRenderer` draws the new `RestrictedLookupReference` only for `absent`: a lock, the label, and no `ReferencedRecordLink`. In a multi-value cell, only the entry that was actually read gets it. That is the first primitive, as before; the overflow chip's `title` lists the label, not the id.
- **No new read.** The label comes from the same read the cell already made, so it reveals nothing the id did not. The platform answers "hidden from you" and "does not exist" with the same 404 on purpose (existence non-disclosure, objectui#8631), so this face is drawn for both. The code comments say so.
- Still loading, read failed, unnamed record, array entries never asked, and an empty value all render as before. A readable lookup still shows its name as a link.
- New key `detail.restrictedLookupReference` in all ten locale packs, read with an inline `defaultValue` so `check:i18n-keys` judges it against the `en` value.
- The docblocks that listed "the resolver answered with no record" as one of the unresolved causes are updated, and so is the header of the objectui#8695 test file.

## Tests (head `05daab07f`)

- New `packages/fields/src/__tests__/lookupCell.restrictedRecord-13335.test.tsx`, 9 tests. Restricted cases: no id in the text or in any attribute, no anchor even with a host `recordHref`, exactly one `findOne`, no `find`; the `en` label with no provider and the `zh` label under `I18nProvider`; the `find`-only data source; multi-value. Controls: a readable record stays named and linked; the in-flight first paint keeps the unresolved face and then turns restricted once the read settles empty; a thrown read keeps the unresolved face and its id; an empty value keeps `EmptyValue` and makes no read.
- New `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/DetailSection.restrictedLookup-13335.test.tsx`: the real `DetailSection` (record page), with a readable sibling as the control.
- New `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/lookupRestrictedRecord-13335.test.tsx`: the real `ObjectGrid`, with a readable row as the control.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over the three new files, every existing test that touches the lookup display or the unresolved-reference affordance (fields, plugin-detail, plugin-grid, app-shell, plugin-dashboard, plugin-list, plugin-tree, plugin-gantt), and the i18n `all-locales-key-parity` and `en-zh-key-parity` tests: **Test Files 67 passed (67), Tests 610 passed (610)**. No existing assertion had to change.
- Ablation: deleting the `absent` return in `useLookupName` (landed on disk through `ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 to 0) turned **8 of the 11 new tests red** in all three files. The 3 that stayed green are the controls (readable, thrown read, empty). The file was restored to the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` was empty afterwards.
- `turbo run type-check` for `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/plugin-grid`: 18/18 tasks successful.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys`, `pnpm check:i18n-drift`, `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys`: all exit 0. Drift reports 1 key added and 0 en values changed.
- eslint on the touched files: 0 errors. `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` has the same warning count as on the base. `check:new-line-citations` reports 0 new. `check-changeset-presence` passes with one changeset.

## Acceptance notes

- **Grid cell wrapper tooltip.** `data-table`'s generic cell wrapper (`packages/components`, outside this card's surface) still puts the raw primitive value in its own `title`. It does that for every primitive cell, so a restricted lookup cell shows the id if you hover the empty space beside the label. The label itself, its own `title`, and the cell's text carry no id, and the grid pin asserts exactly that. Removing the wrapper title for renderer-owned cells would change every custom-cell column, so it is left to the seat.
- **403 is not covered.** A read that throws, including a 403, keeps today's unresolved face. Only the contract's "not found" (`null`) is read as restricted. The card measured a 404, and telling a 403 apart would mean sniffing transport errors inside `@object-ui/fields`.
- **A dangling reference also reads "Restricted record".** When the target was deleted, the server sends the same 404 it sends for a hidden record, so the client cannot tell them apart and the card's wording covers both.

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)
